headline: Gas crisis to be resolved within 5-7 days, says PM Tarique
summary: The Prime Minister attributed the supply disruption to an accident during LNG unloading and blamed the previous government for failing to explore local gas.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman announced that the ongoing gas crisis in Bangladesh will be resolved within the next five to seven days. He attributed the recent supply disruptions to an accident that hampered the unloading of imported liquefied natural gas (LNG).
Speaking at a rally at Pehelgazi Dighi ground in Fatikchhari, the Prime Minister stated that the problem has now been resolved and the supply will stabilize shortly.

PM Tarique blamed the previous government for failing to allow state-owned BAPEX to carry out adequate gas exploration. He claimed that neighbouring countries have been extracting gas from Bangladesh's share due to these unplanned decisions.
During the visit, the Prime Minister met with Hefazat-e-Islam Bangladesh chief Allama Shah Muhibbullah Babunagari at Al-Jamiatul Islamia Azizul Uloom Babunagar Madrasa.
Hefazat-e-Islam submitted a nine-point charter of demands to the Prime Minister, including the recognition of Dawra-e-Hadith degrees and the withdrawal of cases against Islamic scholars.
The Prime Minister expressed his expectation that the organisation will continue to support his government to maintain peace and stability in the country.
The Prime Minister also touched upon the country's political situation, stating that those who tried to steer the country off course during previous elections had failed because of public resistance.
caption:
The gas crisis will be over in 5 to 7 days. PM Tarique Rahman explains why it happened and who is to blame.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman announced that the ongoing gas crisis in Bangladesh will be resolved within the next five to seven days. He attributed the recent supply disruptions to an accident that hampered the unloading of imported liquefied natural gas (LNG).

Speaking at a rally at Pehelgazi Dighi ground in Fatikchhari, the Prime Minister stated that the problem has now been resolved and the supply will stabilize shortly.

PM Tarique blamed the previous government for failing to allow state-owned BAPEX to carry out adequate gas exploration. He claimed that neighbouring countries have been extracting gas from Bangladesh's share due to these unplanned decisions.

During the visit, the Prime Minister met with Hefazat-e-Islam Bangladesh chief Allama Shah Muhibbullah Babunagari at Al-Jamiatul Islamia Azizul Uloom Babunagar Madrasa.

Hefazat-e-Islam submitted a nine-point charter of demands to the Prime Minister, including the recognition of Dawra-e-Hadith degrees and the withdrawal of cases against Islamic scholars.

The Prime Minister expressed his expectation that the organisation will continue to support his government to maintain peace and stability in the country.

The Prime Minister also touched upon the country's political situation, stating that those who tried to steer the country off course during previous elections had failed because of public resistance.

Source: The Daily Star, Dhaka Tribune, Jamuna TV, Prothom Alo
